description: The repository contained only README.md at the start; no code, data, workflows or site existed.
impact: No prior implementation to review; all site content is new.
action: Confirm the repo audit line by line.

description: The 2026 standings page heading renders the literal text '$year$ NFL $displayname$ Standings'.
impact: Possible partially rendered official page; re-check before relying on the heading.
action: Re-fetch and compare division/conference standings views.

description: On the Week 10 injury report most rows publish neither an injury description nor a game status.
impact: Availability signals cannot use those blank fields.
action: Use the final Game Status Report and official inactives instead.

description: The injury page lists 'Seahawks: No Injuries Reported' while an NFL.com news headline on the same page says Sam Darnold was ruled out for Week 10.
impact: Two official surfaces disagree on availability.
action: Pre-register which official surface is authoritative.

description: The injury report lists Puka Nacua as DNP with blank injury and game status, while an NFL.com news headline on the same page says he is likely to be placed on IR.
impact: Injury severity is under-reported in the tabular report.
action: Join news and inactives to the tabular report.

description: Chiefs and Packers depth charts are labelled 'Unofficial' by the clubs themselves.
impact: 2nd/3rd/4th-string assignments are not league-certified.
action: Ask for a league-published depth chart or use official inactives.

description: The 49ers chart says 'Updated as of 11/10/26' but is not labelled 'Unofficial'; the Chiefs chart has no as-of date.
impact: Inconsistent provenance metadata across clubs.
action: Record an as-of label for every snapshot.

description: The league injury report publishes no depth-rank column, and only 3 of 32 clubs' depth charts were transcribed.
impact: Backup-deficiency signals cannot be computed league-wide.
action: Collect all 32 official club depth-chart URLs and snapshot weekly.

description: No official source reviewed publishes NFL betting odds or lines.
impact: Own lines cannot be benchmarked against a verified market line.
action: Request an official odds feed or define a results-only benchmark.

description: No official source publishes leg-level or injury-vs-performance correlation coefficients.
impact: Requested correlation values remain blank except standings-derived ones.
action: Build a game-level panel from official game pages and weekly snapshots.

description: No official source reviewed publishes vig or house edge by bet type.
impact: Break-even thresholds cannot be set.
action: Obtain operator-level odds/hold data from an official regulator dataset.

description: Leaderboard reward values and the ranking formula are not published by any official source.
impact: Reward and score cells are intentionally blank.
action: Pre-register non-monetary rewards and a scoring formula before scoring.

description: Effort and risk estimates for suggestions cannot be confirmed by an official source.
impact: Effort cells are intentionally blank.
action: Record estimates only after a reviewer assigns them.

description: An official page stating the exact game-day inactives deadline was not located in the pages reviewed.
impact: Look-ahead bias boundary is not fully specified.
action: Locate the deadline in the official Game Operations Manual / rulebook.

description: No official NFL gambling-policy document was located on the operations.nfl.com pages reviewed.
impact: Compliance constraints for a betting leaderboard are not fully documented.
action: Request or locate the league's official gambling policy.

description: Session arena-533256e1 claimed 'all' tasks and overlapping scopes including index.html, data/*.csv and docs/*.md.
impact: Risk of duplicate work and conflicting shared outputs.
action: Keep disjoint scopes; integration reconciles shared files.

description: This environment pins the session to one branch, so session-<id>/<task> branches cannot be created.
impact: The brief's branch convention cannot be followed here.
action: Note the deviation; a later session with branch freedom can restructure.

description: Guessed URLs redirected: /the-rules/nfl-rulebook, /inside-football-ops/nfl-operations/integrity-of-the-game, /schedules/2026/REG10.
impact: Using non-canonical links would produce stale citations.
action: Canonical URLs are used in the source registry.

description: 2026 standings show clubs with 8 or 9 games played at the snapshot date.
impact: Raw PF/PA totals are not directly comparable across clubs.
action: Use per-game values in any derived metric; method is shown.

description: The official roster page shows status codes (ACT, RES, DEV, TRC, CUT) without publishing their definitions on that page.
impact: Roster status cannot be interpreted from that page alone.
action: Locate official status-code definitions before using them.

description: The official NJ report describes 2019 New Jersey bettors across all sports, not current NFL-only bettors.
impact: Loss percentages are evidence of structure, not of current NFL strategy performance.
action: Obtain current, NFL-specific official data before calibration.

description: Two different COORDINATION.md boards exist on two active branches.
impact: Task status is not globally consistent.
action: Integration session must reconcile the boards without discarding either.

description: Pages uses a legacy branch build from main / '/'; Jekyll processing must be disabled for plain HTML.
impact: An unrecognised build step could alter generated pages.
action: A .nojekyll file is committed; build status is checked after merge.

description: The rule 'every table row must have a source link to an official site' is applied to analysis rows by linking the official source that grounds the row's domain; project-only assertions are additionally flagged.
impact: Ensures the rule is enforced without fabricating official support for internal states.
action: Confirm the interpretation on review.

description: The earlier sessions' `data/standings.csv` contains a `rank` 1..32 column; the official standings page publishes no rank column.
impact: The ordinal is a project value, not an official statistic; it must not be presented as verified.
action: Label it as site row order or leave blank; the new standings table omits rank entirely.

description: An independent review found three cited operations.nfl.com URLs returning the NFL 404 page (gameday/nfl-schedule/, gameday/, the-rules/).
impact: Those citations cannot be used as evidence on the preserved legacy pages.
action: Use the canonical 2026 rulebook and NFL.com schedule links; legacy pages remain labelled historical.

description: Two preserved legacy pages state that no NFL dataset or injury status was imported, which became stale after the earlier sessions' data pull requests.
impact: Reviewers could read contradictory statements across the two site generations.
action: The new dashboard is authoritative; legacy pages are preserved at legacy-site.html and clearly labelled.

description: Two complete navigation systems now exist in one published site (root dashboard and preserved pages/ site).
impact: Users may see different layouts depending on the entry point.
action: The landing dashboard links explicitly to the preserved site and to the combined-integration page.

description: The earlier sessions' `data/teams.csv` and `data/standings.csv` use `LAR` for the Los Angeles Rams; the standings snapshot transcribed in `data/standings.json` uses the official NFL.com abbreviation `LA`.
impact: Two project snapshots refer to the same club with different abbreviations. Neither value was inferred; both were copied from official pages as rendered at different times.
action: The combined verifier maps LA↔LAR as an alias for comparison, preserves both spellings in their original files, and flags the discrepancy here.

description: Sessions `25aa7696` and `7600ed8b` merged `data/verified/*`, `analysis/*`, `scripts/verified/*` and six new `pages/*.html` files containing 136 official game results, own lines, computed correlations, backtests and a luck analysis.
impact: These are additional deliverables for the same brief. This integration session preserved them all and re-verified the standings, injuries and game results line by line; model-derived numbers were not re-derived here.
action: See integration.html for the cross-checks and links to the preserved pages. Their CI numeric audit is retained.

description: This dashboard publishes six Pearson correlations computed from the 32 official standings rows; the third-generation pages publish four correlations computed from 136 official game results.
impact: Both sets are computed from official data but answer different questions. Neither fills the other's blank cells.
action: Requested leg-level, injury-to-performance and QB/WR correlations remain blank; do not substitute an adjacent metric.

description: The third-generation `pages/lines.html` publishes Week 10 model margins and totals with an explicit FAIL validation verdict; this dashboard's own-line pipeline remains a design with no implemented line values.
impact: A reviewer could mistake the preserved model lines for a validated betting recommendation.
action: The preserved page states the model does not beat its baselines with 95% confidence; no strategy on the leaderboard has passed all gates.

description: The third-generation availability page states that NFL.com team depth-chart URLs return 404 and that depth order is unknown; this dashboard transcribes 1st–4th strings from three official club sites (chiefs.com, packers.com, 49ers.com).
impact: Two official-source classes disagree in coverage: league depth-chart URLs vs club-published unofficial depth charts.
action: Both are preserved with source links; club pages are labelled "Unofficial" by their publishers. Do not generalise three clubs to all 32.

description: There are now multiple Suggestions, Questions, Flagged and Executive Summary pages across the two site generations.
impact: A reviewer may compare different versions without knowing which is authoritative.
action: The landing dashboard is the integration entry point; integration.html links every preserved page and explains the generations.

description: The earlier sessions found three defects (#6, #7, #8) only by reading the live Pages site after a green CI run: an empty evidence table, empty table cells and literal markdown emphasis.
impact: Automated link/number checks do not prove a rendered page reads correctly.
action: This integration fetches the deployed URL and reads the landing page as a user before declaring done; the earlier sessions added gates to check_site.py for all three defect classes.

description: The independent referee session (PR #11) reports that `pages/analysis.html` and `data/verified/model/correlations.json` count 52 division games in Weeks 1-9 where official groupings give 42; it computes a corrected correlation of -0.1048 rather than -0.1297.
impact: A published correlation might be affected; this integration session does not edit another session's files or recompute their model.
action: Fixed by session 08e0ce01: analysis/correlations.py now keys the division flag on conference + division. Reproduced both numbers independently (word-only: 52 games, r=-0.1297; official groupings: 42 games, r=-0.1048) and verified all eight official groupings against https://www.nfl.com/standings/division/2026/REG (2026-11-12). correlations.json and pages/analysis.html regenerated; audit_numbers.py now gates C5 against the official groupings (47 recomputations, all reproduce).

description: The published landing page (index.html) linked only to pages/*: the root section pages (requirements.html, strategy-lab.html, leaderboard.html, bet-types.html, depth-chart.html, data-tables.html, verification.html, integration.html, deployment.html, executive-summary.html, questions.html, suggestions.html, injuries.html, flagged.html, legacy-site.html) and the referee/ and verified-lab/ sub-sites had no inbound link from the landing navigation, so a reader could not reach them by clicking. Found by crawling every href in index.html and pages/*.html,2026-11-12.
impact: Sections required by the brief - most visibly the full requirements inventory - were one click unreachable from the published landing page; check_site.py only enforces reachability inside index.html + pages/*, which is why the gate stayed green.
action: Fixed by session 08e0ce01: added pages/sections.html, a categorized index of every published section (all four site generations plus both sub-sites), linked from the landing navigation. The flat header nav was left otherwise unchanged so no other session's layout was disturbed.

description: CI job 'Verify NFL1 site' runs tools/build.py, which regenerates index.html from a different template (site/templates/base.html, sidebar layout) than the published landing page (pipeline/gen_site.py, header layout), and tools/verify.py then audits the regenerated substitute. The committed landing page is therefore never the page that tools/verify.py checks; it is covered only by scripts/verified/check_site.py and audit_numbers.py.
impact: A defect unique to the published landing page could pass the tools/verify.py gate. Found by diffing a local CI run against the committed tree, 2026-11-12.
action: Logged, not changed: making CI verify the published generation touches shared workflows and two generators' ownership. Published as suggestion S23 for a reviewer to choose a path.

description: Committed generated artifacts lagged their generators: data/combined_verification.json recorded 1,064 audited links where the current audit checks 1,159; the root sidebar pages were missing two navigation entries; index.html still showed 'Data built 05:07' after the data bot committed a refresh at 18:53 that changed the official injury report from 254 rows / 103 starters flagged / 4 clubs without a report to 276 rows / 113 starters flagged / 2 clubs (BAL, LAC).
impact: The published site understated the current official injury report. Verified against the live page on 2026-11-12: Week 10 tables match row-for-row on spot checks, CIN and SEA now publish reports, and the Monday LAC/BAL game reads 'No Injuries Reported' for both clubs.
action: Regenerated by session 08e0ce01 (verify_combined -> build -> gen_site -> build_site -> normalize_nav) so committed pages match current data; suggestion S24 proposes a commit-back or staleness gate so this cannot recur.

description: Data-bot commits carry [skip ci], so verify.yml and pages.yml never run on them: check-runs on bot commit c09c739 are only report-build-status, deploy and build (Pages). Refreshed data therefore reaches main without the verification gates until the next human push.
impact: The 18:53 refresh that changed the official injury report (254 -> 276 rows) landed ungated; the published pages only caught up when this session regenerated them (flag F39).
action: Logged for review: the skip also prevents the bot looping on its own commits, so the fix needs a chosen mechanism (gated refresh). Published as pipeline suggestion S13 and root suggestion S24; this session did not change the workflow unilaterally.

description: COORDINATION.md began with the stray text 'EAD' on line 1 — a leftover conflict-resolution artifact from an earlier merge.
impact: FIXED by session b6e68100; removed in the claim commit. Cosmetic, but it made the board's first heading unreadable to strict parsers.
action: Line-1 artefact removed; board content unchanged. Source: https://github.com/kanlerxz87-cyber/NFL1/blob/main/COORDINATION.md

description: data/model/snapshot.json published WAS winning percentage as 0.312 (float banker's rounding of 0.3125) while the official standings page shows 0.313. The hand-transcribed data/verified/standings_2026.csv already matched the official 0.313, and the stale 0.312 never rendered on any live page.
impact: FIXED in pipeline/build_all.py with exact integer round-half-up arithmetic matching the official convention. The corrected snapshot lands automatically via the collect-data workflow (triggers on pipeline/ changes).
action: Verification source: https://www.nfl.com/standings/league/2026/reg (WAS 2-5-1 shown as 0.313, fetched 2026-11-12); audit trail in docs/audit-b6e68100.md §A2.

description: Week-10 official injury report has 26 club tables. All six absent clubs are now explained from official sources: CHI, DEN, PHI, TB are on bye (official Week-10 schedule page); LAC and BAL print 'No Injuries Reported' on the official injury page.
impact: Supersedes the uncertainty in F11 (absence-of-rows no longer conflates on-bye, no-injuries-reported and scrape-failure). Consumers should treat absent bye clubs as expected, not as a scrape gap.
action: Sources: https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-10 and https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ (both fetched 2026-11-12); audit trail in docs/audit-b6e68100.md §A-F03.

description: The official injury page changes during the day: between the 18:53 UTC scrape (276 rows) and the 22:30 UTC scrape (279 rows), IND statuses changed (Haulcy, Taylor, Tillery, Ward) and 3 rows were added league-wide (CJ Allen, Grover Stewart on IND; BJ Green II on JAX). The scraper was verified faithful (~120 rows compared row-for-row against the live page, 0 errors).
impact: Site injury data is a dated snapshot that can lag the official page by hours. Decision reads shortly before kickoff should re-scrape; the daily 11:17 UTC refresh alone is insufficient on game day.
action: Discovery suggestion logged on the Suggestions page (SA-02): add a scheduled pre-slate refresh. Source: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ (fetched 2026-11-12); audit trail in docs/audit-b6e68100.md §A-F04.

category: Standings snapshot vs live page (currency note)
description: Live recheck 2026-11-13: 30 of 32 standing rows match every published file exactly. NYG and WAS differ only because the Week-10 TNF game (Commanders 24, Giants 21, FINAL, Thu Nov 12) finished after every file's recorded retrieval (2026-11-12T04:31Z..23:37Z). The delta is arithmetically exact (+21/+24 PF-PA NYG, +24/+21 WAS) and all six files agree with each other on pre-game values.
impact: Readers comparing the site to nfl.com after Thursday night will see two stale rows. Not a data error; the daily collect refresh folds results in.
action: Sources: https://www.nfl.com/standings/league/2026/reg and https://www.nfl.com/games/commanders-at-giants-2026-reg-10 (fetched 2026-11-13); diff in data/audit/live_recheck_2026-11-13/standings_diff.json; audit docs/audit-65df4799.md §1.

category: KC depth chart rows disagree with the club page
description: Live recheck 2026-11-13 of the 28 KC rows: 25 exact. Still differing: Offense WR row 2 (club: 2nd Cyrus Allen, 3rd Josh Downs; repo: s2 blank, s3 Cyrus Allen, Josh Downs absent) and KR/PR (club: 1st Emmett Johnson, 2nd Cyrus Allen; repo: s1 blank, s2 Emmett Johnson). DT row 1 (Chris Jones/Peter Woods) now matches and that part of X09 is resolved. The club labels its chart 'Unofficial Depth Chart'.
impact: Down-2/3rd-string deficiency reads for KC are wrong on three rows (WR2, KR, PR). X09 and R-6a232e79-03 stay open until data/depth_chart.json is re-transcribed by its owner.
action: Source: https://www.chiefs.com/team/depth-chart (fetched 2026-11-13); comparison in docs/audit-65df4799.md §4. Not silently corrected (no-silent-correction rule).

category: Two generators wrote pages/lines.html (fixed in this session)
description: pipeline/gen_site.py ('My Lines') and scripts/verified/build_site.py ('Own Lines') both wrote pages/lines.html; whichever ran last silently replaced the page. tools/check_generators.py could not see it because its regex missed the builder's page dict.
impact: The live landing page's 'My Lines' link could show the wrong document depending on build order. Fixed: the verified sub-site page is now pages/verified-lines.html, the ownership map records both, and the gate detects dict-key claims.
action: Fix commit on this branch (integration merge 2026-11-13); gate: tools/check_generators.py PASS with both owners recorded.

category: Broken nav links on pages/availability.html (fixed in this session)
description: scripts/verified/build_availability.py passed a bare page name to the renderer, so all 21 nav links on pages/availability.html were written root-style (pages/x.html from inside pages/) and were broken.
impact: Every navigation link on the Availability page 404'd. Fixed by passing the pages/-qualified name; check_committed_site and the verified check_site now report 0 broken links.
action: Fix commit on this branch; re-verified with tools/check_committed_site.py and scripts/verified/check_site.py.

category: News-to-status gap in the availability model
description: Sam Darnold (SEA): the official report row shows Did Not Participate with a blank game status while official news says he is ruled out for Week 10. Both are official; the model carries no news column, so the row under-states the absence.
impact: Starter-availability and next-man-up reads can be too optimistic whenever news outruns the game-status column (R-6a232e79-07).
action: Sources: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ (row) and https://www.nfl.com/news/sam-darnold-ruled-out-for-seahawks-week-10-game-vs-raiders-drew-lock-expected-to-start-again (both fetched 2026-11-13). Feature request S28 filed.

description: Live recheck 2026-11-13 read the full official Week-10 report (296 rows, 26 clubs) and compared every field with data/model/official_injuries.json: 296/296 match. All rows previously flagged as missing or extra (X01 IND practice cells; X02 BJ Green II/CJ Allen/Grover Stewart; RV-02 Jaydn Ott/Kendal Daniels/Jawaan Taylor/Cameron Thomas) are present and match the live page. LAC and BAL print 'No Injuries Reported'.
impact: Confirms the scrape is faithful and the earlier discrepancies were page drift between scrape times (A-F04), not parser corruption. RV-02/X01/X02 can be closed by their owners.
action: Source: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ (all 7 chunks fetched 2026-11-13); audit docs/audit-65df4799.md §3.

description: The committed standings snapshot (retrieved 2026-11-12T04:31Z from https://www.nfl.com/standings/league/2026/reg) shows NYG 5-2-1, PF 182, PA 172 and WAS 2-5-1, PF 172, PA 202. The same official page fetched 2026-11-13 shows NYG 5-3-1, PF 203, PA 196 and WAS 3-5-1, PF 196, PA 223. The change matches the WAS @ NYG game played 2026-11-12, after the snapshot was taken: the snapshot is not wrong, it is dated, and the live page keeps moving.
impact: Any comparison between the committed data and the live official page must quote retrieved_at, or the difference looks like a data error. No decision should use the older values as current.
action: Re-snapshot the official standings page after each Sunday slate and quote retrieved_at beside every published standings value; treat same-week changes as drift, not error (see also A-F04 for injury-page drift). Source: https://www.nfl.com/standings/league/2026/reg.

description: The Week-11 refresh of data/model/snapshot.json (generated 2026-11-13T13:04Z from the upstream schedules feed) listed JAX @ NYG at 13:00 and PIT @ PHI at 16:25. The official Week-11 page, read 2026-11-13, shows Jaguars at Giants 4:25 PM ET (16:25) and Steelers at Eagles 1:00 PM ET (13:00): the two kickoff times were swapped with each other in the feed, and the snapshot rows cite the official schedule as their source, so the values contradicted their own citation.
impact: A wrong kickoff time on a betting-decision page changes which games are live when. tools/verify_official.py check B3 caught the mismatch against the official capture.
action: Fixed: the two snapshot values were corrected to the official times and pipeline/build_all.py now applies a documented, source-linked SCHEDULE_FEED_FIXES table at build time so scheduled refreshes keep the official values. Reviewer: confirm against https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-11 and https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/REG11 (fetched 2026-11-13); if the upstream feed is corrected, the table can be dropped (it is idempotent).

description: data/model/official_injuries.json holds 345 Week-10 rows (scrape generated 2026-11-14T17:02:31Z from https://www.nfl.com/injuries/). Every row populates team (for example WAS, NE) but no club field is present on any row, and counts.clubs_resolved_from_roster is 0, so the club foreign key is not resolved. Downstream joins that key off club (roster, depth chart, snap counts) would match nothing. Spot-checked 12 rows against the live official page on 2026-11-15: all matched (Patrick/Yankoff Out, Harrison Questionable, Brown/Davis III/Henderson Out, Joseph/Mays/Reed Out, Darnold Out). Row count is a live-week snapshot and drifts within the week (see A-F04).
impact: Availability/roster joins keyed on club return zero rows until club resolution is added; not a values error in the scraped fields themselves.
action: Resolve club from the team code or the club table at scrape time, backfill counts.clubs_resolved_from_roster, and add a per-refresh row-count gate against https://www.nfl.com/injuries/.

category: Official results corpus is one game behind standings
description: The verified results corpus contains 136 games and ends at Week 9. The official 2026 standings retrieved 2026-11-13 sum to 136 wins, 136 losses and 2 ties, implying 137 completed games. The official Week 10 Game Center reports Commanders 24, Giants 21, FINAL on 2026-11-12. The result is not present in data/verified/games_2026.csv. No score row has been added by this audit.
impact: The verified backtest results corpus is incomplete at its stated current-season boundary. Historical skill metrics, result verification and any injury/result join are blocked for the omitted game until its official Game Book and provenance are captured and reconciled.
action: Reconcile the official Game Center and NFL Game Book with the registered 2026 results corpus, record the official game ID, final score, source URL, captured timestamp and hash, then rerun the result and leaderboard gates. Official schedule: https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-10. Keep the affected row blank until verified.

description: The committed scrape (data/model/official_injuries.json, generated 2026-11-14T17:02Z) has no injury or game status where the live nfl.com read (2026-11-15) shows one: Chargers, 10 injury and 10 game-status cells, and 6 practice-status values; Ravens, 2 injury and 2 game-status cells (Jaylinn Hawkins: Knee, Out; Adam Randall: Neck, Hamstring, Questionable). The parser stored blanks without any error. Chargers example from the live page: David Njoku, Fibula, Questionable.
impact: Two clubs are published with missing injury designations. The rule against publishing blanks is broken, and no alarm fired.
action: Re-run the scrape with the raw HTML kept for the LAC and BAL sections; fix the column mapping; add the drift alarm (SI-09). Compare with data/brief_07810d9f/injury_delta_2026-11-15.json.
resolution: Resolved in the committed data. data/model/official_injuries.json matches the dated 2026-11-15 capture on every row (347/347, zero value differences). The Chargers (LAC, 19 rows) and Ravens (BAL, 10 rows) sections were re-read in full on https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ on 2026-11-15 and match cell for cell (e.g. David Njoku, Fibula, Questionable; Jaylinn Hawkins, Knee, Out; Adam Randall, Neck, Hamstring, Questionable).

description: Two Ravens rows on the live nfl.com read are absent from the committed scrape: Calais Campbell (DT, Did Not Participate In Practice) and Ronnie Stanley (Did Not Participate In Practice). The cause (a page change between reads, or parser loss) is not determined.
impact: The published Ravens list is 2 players short.
action: Determine from the raw page at the next capture whether the rows were added after 2026-11-14 or dropped by the parser.
resolution: Resolved in the committed data. Calais Campbell (DT, DNP) and Ronnie Stanley (T, DNP) are present in data/model/official_injuries.json and match the Ravens section of https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ read on 2026-11-15. Parser-loss cause still not determined; the row count is recorded per capture (see F-7810-04).

description: Arden Key (IND) carries Hamstring and Questionable in the committed scrape (2026-11-14). The live read (2026-11-15) shows no injury and no game status for him.
impact: A designation disappeared between reads, or the scrape is stale. Either way the published Colts row disagrees with the live page.
action: Keep both reads in the dated series (IN-01) and confirm at the next capture.
resolution: Resolved in the committed data. Arden Key (IND) is committed with no injury and Full Participation; the Colts section of https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ read on 2026-11-15 shows the same. The earlier Hamstring/Questionable read stays in the dated history and is not overwritten.

category: Injury row counts differ across captures
description: Counts for the same nfl.com page differ by capture: 296 rows across 26 clubs (official check, 2026-11-13, per the landing page note); 345 rows in the committed scrape (2026-11-14); 347 rows across 28 clubs in the live read (2026-11-15). CHI, DEN, PHI and TB have no rows on the live read.
impact: No single Week 10 count can be cited. Each count must carry its capture date.
action: Publish every count with its capture time (done for 2026-11-15 in the register); do not overwrite earlier counts.

description: The Houston Texans depth chart page (read 2026-11-15) is labelled 'Unofficial Depth Chart' and holds an image in place of text. The depth ladder has no Houston slots (chart_status 'unavailable').
impact: The 32-club depth sweep is 31 of 32. Houston depth and any Houston team-level model are blocked.
action: Find an authorized structured source (club or NFL text feed). Do not transcribe the image by eye.

category: Jersey numbers left in depth rows
description: data/depth_chart.json still holds jersey numbers in 59 Packers cells (a leading number before the player name). The brief requires the numbers stripped and the raw string kept.
impact: Packers names are mis-keyed in any join on player name.
action: Strip the leading number into its own column; keep the raw string; re-run the name join.
resolution: Resolved. Script: tools/normalize_depth_names.py strips the leading jersey number from 59 Packers cells into jersey_s1..s4, keeps the printed string in raw_s1..s4, and leaves s1..s4 as bare names. The numbers and names were checked against https://www.packers.com/team/depth-chart read on 2026-11-15 (footer: 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'). The club label is unchanged and still flagged under F-7810-07.

description: Three official club charts carry an 'Unofficial' label on the club's own page: Chiefs ('Unofficial Depth Chart', S14), Packers ('Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026', S15) and Texans (S30). The repo treats club charts as official for that club.
impact: Whether a club chart counts as an official source is a decision, not a fact. The brief asks for official depth; some charts describe themselves as unofficial.
action: Record the decision on the Decide page: accept the club chart as official for that club, or require a different official source.

category: Baltimore QB depth: stale-listing item resolved

description: NFL.com Terms and Conditions (updated May 16, 2024; https://www.nfl.com/legal/terms/) s.1.1 prohibit copying, reproducing, distributing or displaying Services content for any purpose except as the Agreement expressly allows. s.1.3 limits use to 'your own individual non-commercial and informational purposes' and states that 'systematic retrieval of data or other content from the Services, whether to create or compile ... a collection, compilation, database, or directory, is prohibited absent our express prior written consent'. This repository systematically retrieves https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ every 6 hours (data/snapshots/injury_report/) and the schedule and standings pages, and publishes row-level player names and designations (347 injury rows, roughly 21 public pages, including the Injury Snapshots page and data/model/official_injuries.json). No written consent is on file. The repository's own rule is that raw row-level data stays in a private store until the terms are read; the terms are now read and they restrict this use.
impact: Legal and licence exposure for the public site and for the snapshot pipeline. Not a values error: the published numbers match the official page. The fix is a product decision: (a) obtain written consent from NFL Enterprises, LLC, (b) keep row-level nfl.com content in a private store and publish only aggregate counts and links to the official page, or (c) remove the scrape. This session did not remove any published content, so the decision is left to the owner.
action: Owner decision before the next scheduled capture. Legal review is recommended. Option (b) is the smallest change: the snapshot page would show counts and deltas and link to https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ for names.

description: data/readiness.json (decision-readiness rows R1-R10, built by tools/build_readiness.py) cited https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-10 as the source of six rows (R1, R2, R3, R4, R9, R10). Those rows report backtest results, two-leg parlay tests, strategy registration hashes, the demotion rule and bet price records. No official page holds those numbers, and the NFL schedule page does not contain them, so the citation did not support the row. The rows now link to the repository file that computes them, labelled 'internal computation: no official source applies'. R6 (club depth charts) was cited to nfl.com/injuries and now links to data/depth_ladder.json, which holds the per-club official chart links. Separately, data/depth_ladder.json contains an unresolved template URL, https://www.<club>/team/depth-chart, which is not a real page.
impact: The readiness table no longer presents internal numbers as official. Six rows have no official source by design: an official page cannot confirm a backtest. Nothing on the published page is inferred from the schedule.
action: Replace the template URL in data/depth_ladder.json with each club's real chart URL, or remove it. Decide whether the registration and demotion rules need a non-official record (they are internal policy, so no official page can confirm them).

description: Backtest returns and hit rates still appear on other pages after the leaderboard was split: the research executive summary (research/executive-summary.html, gate summary table with a Return column), the research injuries page (research/injuries.html, scored-rule table with Return and p-value), the root-site strategies page (pages/strategies.html) and the decision dashboard strategies page (dashboard/strategies.html). action: Decide whether these pages should carry the same split (figures moved to a labelled backtest view). Then apply the same test to each page.

category: Terms of use: clauses beyond F51
description: Read in full on 2026-11-16 (data/legal/terms_2026-11-16.json). Four clauses bear on this repository and are not covered by F51: s.8 'For any other type of link to the Services, you must obtain our express written permission' (the site deep-links to nfl.com injury, schedule and transaction pages); s.11(f) prohibits using 'spiders, robots' or 'agent[s]' to 'harvest or otherwise collect information from the Services to be used for any commercial purpose'; s.12 prohibits 'using the Services to gamble or wager on the result of any NFL game'; and s.2 lets NFL change the text at any time. Section 11(d) also prohibits any action that 'imposes an unreasonable or disproportionately large load'. No load measurement is in the repository.
impact: The repository's stated purpose is wagering strategy on NFL games. Whether s.12 covers use of nfl.com data for that purpose is a legal question. This session does not decide it. Deep links need written permission under the text as written, or a reading that they are covered by s.8's first sentence.
action: Counsel or the repository owner to read s.8, s.11(f) and s.12 against the planned use before the next publication. Decide whether to request NFL's written consent, and whether to link only to the home page.

Against that: data/session-1505ac8e/depth_charts.json holds 31 of 32 clubs with 934 position rows and 1990 slots (HOU unavailable, captured 2026-11-12T23:17Z), and data/depth/official_register.json holds official club-page captures pinned at GB 55 / KC 60 / SF 58 / SEA 63 rows. Two clubs' worth of the register is 4 pages, not 32, so both statements are partly true and both are published as if total.
impact: The site simultaneously claims no depth data exists and holds per-slot depth rows. A reader cannot tell which artifact a depth number came from, which is what the ablation requirement needs to be measurable.
action: pick one register as the depth source of truth, say in the text how many clubs it covers, and replace "none exists" with the coverage count

category: The league's transactions page prints at most 25 rows per month
description: https://www.nfl.com/transactions/league/<category>/<year>/<month> prints the 25 most recent rows of that month and no more. Verified on 2026-11-16: adding ?page=2 to reserve-list/2026/11 returns the same 25 rows, and a per-day url (/transactions/league/reserve-list/2026/11/14) returns 404. So a month whose oldest printed row is later than the first of the month is a partial view at the source: 15 of the 24 captured pages were in that state on 2026-11-16, and the pages for months that have already closed cannot be completed by re-reading them.
impact: Any monthly or season-long turnover count is a floor, not a total. The register handles the running month by taking the union of every capture (the hourly sweep keeps rows from disappearing when they slide out of the window), and the published page labels capped months explicitly. Closed months before the sweep started are permanently short.
status: Open - disclosed on the site, not repaired
action: if season-complete turnover is required, source it from an official publication that prints whole months (Game Books or the league's own transaction PDFs); do not present a capped month as a total

category: Freshness gate treats an evidence file's self-reported capture time as an expiry
description: tools/check_freshness.py compares a generated file's stamp with the 'captured_at' stamp an evidence file reports for itself, so any session that touches an evidence file's captured_at turns the freshness gate red for everyone even though no data moved. Demonstrated on 2026-11-16: the gate failed on main with 'decision_room/decision_room.json is older than its inputs (data/evidence/injuries_week10.json, standings_2026.json, official_verification.json)'; running the two builders the gate prescribes (tools/build_decision_room.py, tools/build_dashboard.py) changed NEITHER of their outputs - both regenerated byte-identical - and the only diff left in the tree was 'captured_at' on six data/evidence files whose content was hand-transcribed on 2026-11-13 and was not re-read. Those stamps were reverted rather than committed, because publishing a capture time that is not the capture time is exactly what the source-of-truth rules forbid. The gate then passes: the canonical build (tools/build_site_all.py), which the collect job runs, re-stamps the decision-room artifact, so the red is cleared by rebuilding the site, not by re-reading a source.
impact: Between the stale stamp and the next full build, the Collect job on main is red for every session, which is how a real model-rebuild failure gets lost; and the cheapest way to silence it is stamp churn on evidence files, which would falsify a capture time. The gate should therefore not treat a self-reported input timestamp as an expiry.
action: owner decision on tools/check_freshness.py: compare content hashes rather than stamps so an unchanged input cannot make an output stale; and have the decision-room builder preserve its inputs' captured_at instead of relying on a re-run. Do not 'fix' a freshness failure by bumping captured_at without re-reading the official source.

category: Check E passes now, but the frozen corpus is still 12 games behind the season
description: When this session claimed (main 46c82ae) tools/verify_official.py check E failed: it compared data/model/dashboard.json counts.games_played (137) with half the sum of club games in data/evidence/standings_current.json (149). An upstream data refresh merged to main while this session ran (commit e2f9916) raised the dashboard count to the official 149, so check E now PASSES: 149 games, 0 of 28 checks failing, report data/audit/official_verification.json generated 2026-11-16T18:05:02Z. The underlying data gap is unchanged: the frozen backtest corpus data/s9cb/games.csv still holds 137 results and only one Week-10 final (WAS 24-21 NYG); 12 of the 13 Week-10 finals are absent from it. The gate went green because the dashboard was corrected to match the official count, not because the corpus caught up.
impact: The failing job is cleared, so the build is no longer red. The model's ratings, own lines and every backtest still sit on a corpus 12 games behind the season, so published accuracy figures describe a slightly earlier state than the season the page describes.
status: Open - gate green, corpus still behind; disclosed on the site, not repaired
action: Freeze a new corpus_id from a refreshed results feed. Do not edit the pre-registered corpus in place. The gate is a live read on the desk pages, so it will flip to a failure again if the dashboard count and the official standings ever disagree.

category: Three committed copies of the official standings no longer match the page
description: data/standings.json (read 2026-11-12), data/s9cb/official_standings_2026.csv (2026-11-12) and data/personnel/official_standings_2026-11-13.csv (2026-11-13) each reproduce only 6 of 32 club rows against the official table read on 2026-11-16; data/evidence/standings_current.json reproduces 32 of 32. The example: BUF is 7-1 with PF 256 on 2026-11-12 and 8-1 with PF 287 on 2026-11-16.
impact: Pages built from the older copies show a standings table that is three days out of date next to pages built from the fresh one. A reader comparing two pages sees two different records for the same club.
status: Open - disclosed on the site, not repaired
action: Regenerate the three copies from a fresh read, or print the read date in the table caption so the drift is visible. They are owned by other generators, so this session published the comparison instead of editing them.

category: The club code the league prints differs between its own pages, and joins depend on an unpublished crosswalk
description: The injury page and the schedule page print AZ for Arizona; a committed capture of the same injury page normalises it to ARI. nfl.com prints LA for the Rams while the club site prints LAR. Any join across these sources silently depends on a mapping that is not published anywhere on the site.
impact: A join written without the crosswalk drops or duplicates one club's rows. In this session's comparison, 15 of 347 injury rows keyed differently purely because of AZ vs ARI; the rows themselves were identical.
action: Publish the crosswalk (printed code, normalised code, page that prints it) beside every join.

category: The earlier 'three Lions rows have a blank game status' finding is no longer true on the official page
description: The brief states that Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed are published with a blank game-status cell. Re-read on 2026-11-16, all three carry game status Out (Joseph, knee; Mays, ankle; Reed, hip). The blank cells exist in an older hand copy in data/capture/, not on the page.
impact: A published finding now contradicts its own source. Left uncorrected it would send a reader to 'fix' a page that is already correct.
action: No action on the source. The older finding is superseded; the stale hand copy is still in the repo and should be labelled.

category: The stale-depth finding about Baltimore is resolved at source
description: The brief records that Baltimore still publishes Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at QB after both went on injured reserve. The chart re-read on 2026-11-16 lists Jacoby Brissett, Joe Fagnano and Kedon Slovis at QB, and the dated official transactions register carries '11/06 AZ BAL Jacoby Brissett Traded'.

category: Depth data covers 3 of 32 clubs on this page, and one of the three attaches no date
description: This session transcribed the Detroit, Baltimore and Green Bay charts. Green Bay prints 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'; Detroit prints 'Compiled by Lions Football Communications' with no date; Baltimore prints no date. The other 29 clubs are absent. The existing register covers 4 clubs, so coverage after this session is 4 of 32, not 3.

status: Open - disclosed on the site, not repaired

category: The Texans publish their depth chart as an image and no structured source is authorised
description: The brief reports that Houston's depth page is an image. This session did not transcribe it: transcribing an image by eye is the one thing the brief forbids. No structured source for Houston depth is present in the repo.

status: Open - disclosed on the site, not repaired

category: One club's depth page prints the jersey number inside the name cell, so a naive parse invents a different player
description: Green Bay prints cells as '9 Christian Watson'. A parse that keeps the cell text produces a name that matches no roster row. This session keeps both: 'raw' holds the printed cell and 'name' holds the stripped name.
impact: A register that stores only the printed cell cannot be joined to a roster or an injury report, and the failure is silent.
action: Keep the raw string and the stripped name side by side in every depth table.

category: A committed depth register keeps rows with an empty name
description: data/depth/official_register.json holds 3 rows for Green Bay whose name field is empty. They are counted as register rows, so the register's row count overstates the number of named players.
impact: A coverage count built on register row count is three rows too high.
status: Open - disclosed on the site, not repaired

category: The site's rendered landing page carries a stale games-played count
description: data/model/dashboard.json, generated 2026-11-15T17:42Z, asserts games_played 137 while the official standings read a day later imply 149. The mismatch is the same one D-F01 records, but it is published on the landing page as a fact rather than as a lag.
impact: The front page states a season length that is 12 games short.

category: Readiness register regeneration reverts other sessions' in-place row edits
description: Running scripts/brief_07810d9f/register.py to regenerate room/data/readiness.json reverts in-place status edits made by other sessions, because register.py is the source of truth for the file and those edits were not written back through it. Demonstrated 2026-11-16: to update one row (MO-04 -> Done) the file was regenerated through register.py, which changed 16 rows and reverted four rows that other sessions had set to Done/Partial (IN-20, IN-22, IN-26, IN-27 from the 1d824ec2 transactions sweep; PR-18, PR-24, PR-25 from the pre-registration and strategy-competition sessions) back to Not started. The regeneration was reverted and the MO-04 row was applied in place instead, so no other session's row was touched.
impact: A session that regenerates the register to update one row silently publishes false 'Not started' statuses for requirements other sessions have built, and the landing-page readiness panel would show them as unbuilt.
action: Owner decision: fold the in-place row edits back into register.py (so the script and the published file agree), then regenerate once; or make register.py merge in-place edits instead of overwriting them. Until then, update readiness rows in place and do not regenerate the whole file from register.py.
